clue.text: Talk endlessly about right look for a girl

indicators.note: the shortened talk word goes around the next pieces, wrapping them
the word for talk loses its final letter, its end cut off

parts.note: to talk idly is to chatter
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone who talks nonstop eyes up the right outfit to win a girl over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look for a girl' reads as searching for someone; 'a girl' is the definition. 'endlessly' trims the last letter of the talk word, and 'about' wraps the shortened word around R and LO.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a common female first name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: In a way, switching off maybe why mouse is jumping around

definitions.text: In a way, switching off maybe

explanation.surface: The reason a mouse is leaping about: something has switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short doze, a way of switching off; and when the cat dozes, the mice are free to play.

clue.text: One's not pro-America and against Europe, no gains in that

parts.note: at can mean against, as in to fly at someone

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to America and Europe gains nothing from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' means professional, not 'in favour of'; 'no gains in that' adds that an amateur is unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part without payment, in contrast to a professional.

clue.text: Used in Kerala, this club

indicators.note: used in says the letters are employed within the words Kerala, this

explanation.surface: In Kerala they use this club.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is found in 'keraLA THIs'; fittingly, it is an Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy stick, often iron-bound, used as a weapon by Indian police.

clue.text: Lofty adult has church office in us capital

parts.note: lofty means tall
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
taken as written
a see is the office or diocese of a bishop

explanation.surface: A tall grown-up holds a church post in the United States capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the USA, not the pronoun; the capital is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallahassee is the state capital of Florida, a capital city within the USA.

clue.text: Part of an address in Sloane square

indicators.note: in says the letters are sitting inside the words sloane square

explanation.surface: Sloane Square forms part of a London address.
explanation.walkthrough: Found in 'sloanE SQuare'. Sloane Square is a smart square in Chelsea, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esq., short for esquire, is a courtesy title written after a man's name in an address.

clue.text: Composer in database heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the database is taken as spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: a list is a simple database of items

explanation.surface: A composer's name turns up in a records system spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Trouble sensed after gents producing items to be settled

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the word for gents

parts.note: the gents is a men's lavatory, and loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: trouble is a verb here, stirring the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Trouble was sensed after someone went to the toilet, leaving things to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' reads as a noun but is a verb stirring up the letters of 'sensed'. The gents is the British word for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are unfinished details still needing to be tidied up.

clue.text: What employee with corporation may want to be

definitions.text: What employee with corporation may want to be

parts.words: What employee with corporation may want to be
parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a large paunch, so a worker with a big belly hopes to lose weight

explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a big company; it is old slang for a fat belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a paunch would want to be thinner, the comparative of slim.

clue.text: Row about Italian raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An Italian raised a row about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RE IT upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row of seats, one of several rising above each other.

clue.text: Pamphlet seen in vehicle or shed

indicators.note: shed is a verb here, casting off the two letters of the next word from the vehicle

parts.note: a tractor is a farm vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaflet is spotted in a car or a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building beside the vehicle; it is the verb 'cast off', removing OR from TRACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political in content.

clue.text: Sweet drink with sorbet

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
a sorbet is a water ice

explanation.surface: A sweet treat: a drink served with a sorbet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is a noun here, a sweet you eat, not an adjective describing the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a black chewy confection, a classic British sweet.

clue.text: Loose madam with nice rear is aspiration abroad

indicators.note: loose suggests letters set free to fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rather risque description of a woman of easy virtue with a pleasing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like a description of the madam, but it is the anagram signal for MADAM, NICE and REAR. 'abroad' places the aspiration in the USA, from the British setter's view.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Dream is the ideal that anyone in the USA can prosper through hard work, a national hope across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Day since reorganised, cricket county is disappointing

indicators.note: reorganised says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county with a first-class cricket team

explanation.surface: Since the day the county cricket side was restructured, it has been a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket county' points to one of the English counties with a first-class cricket side; Hants is the usual short form of Hampshire. 'reorganised' scrambles 'since'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disenchant someone is to disillusion them, letting them down.

clue.text: Big lagers ordered before cold beer

indicators.note: before places the jumbled letters ahead of the rest
ordered says the letters are arranged in a new sequence

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Lagers ordered before a chilled beer make for a big night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like buying drinks at the bar; it rearranges LAGERS to LARGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale means extensive or on a grand scale.

clue.text: On record, agent brought back support for climbers

indicators.note: brought back says the whole run of pieces is turned round, read from end to start

parts.note: A means on, as in 'aboard' or 'once a day', an old prefix sense
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
a rep is a sales representative, an agent for a firm

explanation.surface: A mountaineering agent, going on record, brought back some kit for climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses A LOG REP together, giving PER GOL A. 'climbers' are climbing plants, not mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework of posts and beams over which climbing plants are trained.

clue.text: Utter repeated instructions to quit

explanation.surface: Shouting the command to leave over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or thorough; literally, 'out!' said and said again tells someone to leave.

clue.text: Broadcast recalled after celebrated Spanish drink

indicators.note: after places the reversed broadcast word behind the celebrated word

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it, so celebrated can mean sang

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the broadcast word is turned round

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A programme recalls a famous Spanish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'celebrated' looks like an adjective meaning famous; it is the past tense of a verb, as in singing someone's praises. 'recalled' turns the broadcast word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine mixed with fruit and sometimes brandy.

clue.text: Modern building embraced by numbers making records

indicators.note: embraced by means the building sits inside the abbreviation for numbers

parts.note: Tate Modern is the London gallery of modern art in a former power station

explanation.surface: A new building surrounded by figures is used for keeping records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modern building' looks like any new structure; it is Tate Modern, the London art gallery, so TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write down in notation, so notates means records something in writing.

clue.text: Like the Sunday times in Capitol complex?

indicators.note: complex suggests a tangled arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper in the Capitol building in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a group of buildings; it is the anagram signal for CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical newspaper deals with current affairs, as the Sunday Times does.

clue.text: Horse takes outsize bits of early barley from this?

definitions.text: Horse takes outsize bits of early barley from this?

indicators.note: takes means the horse word holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse
OS is the abbreviation for outsize in clothing

indicators.note: bits of picks the first letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A horse grabs big mouthfuls of early barley from its feeding bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a picture of a horse feeding from the answer, which is why it ends with 'from this?'. 'takes' signals the container, with the horse word as the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feeding bag hung over a horse's head, from which it eats grain.

clue.text: Extend British circle close to Arabian port

indicators.note: close to means the port is placed right beside the circle

parts.note: O is a circle by its shape
Aden is a port in Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A British ring is extended close to an Arabian port.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden is to widen or expand something.

clue.text: Innocent chaps hit for removing vehicles

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are knocked about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Blameless men are struck by some vans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' means 'used for removals', moving house; a PANTECHNICON is the British name for a large furniture removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantechnicons are large vans used by removal firms to carry household furniture.

clue.text: Small key one left in place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the place word

parts.note: to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: A small key that someone left in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a low island, as in the Florida Keys, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a tiny island, and key is a word for a low island or reef.

clue.text: Luggage claims

explanation.surface: Someone claims the luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags are cases for travel; to bag something is to claim it, as in 'bags I go first'.

clue.text: TV presenter with weight on board?

explanation.surface: A heavyweight newsreader joins a television team.
explanation.definitionFit: A news programme's lead presenter is called its anchor; a crewman handling a ship's heavy anchor is, playfully, a man with weight aboard.

clue.text: Cleaner gets work after end of term

indicators.note: after places the work abbreviation behind the picked letter
end of picks the final letter of the word term

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A cleaner gets a job when the school term ends.
explanation.walkthrough: In the answer the letter picked from 'term' comes first and OP follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mop is used to clean floors, so it is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Sparkly diamonds are essential for a lady

indicators.note: are essential for says the letters sit at the core of the words sparkly diamonds

explanation.surface: Glittering gems are a must for any woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is found inside 'sparkLY DIAmonds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name, so it is an example of a lady's name.

clue.text: Separate European resort

explanation.surface: A holiday town split off from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is to part or divide; Split is a resort city on Croatia's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Stick around numbers in cast, for example

indicators.note: around means the word for stick is placed on both sides of the numbers word

parts.note: to paste something is to stick it
tens are numbers, as in counting in tens

explanation.surface: A theatre company's members are glued together for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors in a play; here it is the verb form, since 'cast' is its own past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast is the past form of the verb cast, so it is an example of a grammatical past form.
